title: Dependency Telegraph: signal lifecycle, impact windows, and escalation workflow
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: big-ticket initiatives (runtime releases, Dedicated capacity rollouts, console migrations) repeatedly surface late blockers from infra, security, or design that cause rework and release slippage. Existing dependency spreadsheets and blunt 'owner' fields don't capture urgency, impact window, or the right escalation path.

Goal: build the 'Dependency Telegraph' — a lightweight, team-agnostic lifecycle and signal model that surfaces: impact window, blocking severity, probabilistic readiness estimate, primary/secondary owners, and an automated nudge/escalation path tied to roadmap gates. Provide a console view + Slack nudges + weekly digest so PMs and Eng leads can see where to focus remediations. Pilot on three Q2 initiatives (runtime-1.22 rollout, Console metrics rewrite, Dedicated autoscaling policy).
acceptance_criteria: Console: new dependency row widget showing impact window (start/end), severity (low/med/high), readiness % and last update timestamp
Workflow: automated Slack nudge to primary owner at T-14d, T-7d, T-2d before the impact window; escalation to secondary owner and manager if no update after 48h
API: dependency lifecycle states (Raised, Acknowledged, Mitigating, Blocked, Resolved) exposed via REST endpoint and wired into existing roadmap importer
Pilot: three target initiatives onboarded, with weekly readiness score and a post-pilot retrospective with quantitative metrics (reduction in last-minute blockers by >=40%)
Guidance: published short runbook in Confluence with decision rules for severity assignment and escalation matrix
